question_text: While driving at night on a country road you see pedestrians on your side. What do you do if you are dazzled by an oncoming vehicle?

options.text: Reduce speed and, if necessary, stop
Switch to high beam and proceed without reducing speed
Accelerate in order to get out of the area of dazzle as quickly as possible

correct_answers.text: Reduce speed and, if necessary, stop

comment: If an oncoming vehicle dazzles you, be sure to reduce the speed so you can stop at any time in a potentially dangerous situation. If pedestrians are on or near the lane, you may even need to stop in such cases. Increasing your speed is not allowed.

question_text: What must you do if wild animals suddenly appear in the full beam of your headlights?

options.text: Immediately dip your headlights
Sound the horn and brake
Proceed on full beam

comment: Hold the steering wheel tightly and brake. Dip the high beam, because it dazzles the game and therefore remains on the road. Honk to scare it away. Avoid trying to dodge at high speed. These maneuvers often end at a tree or in oncoming traffic. That's why the following rules apply when there's game on the road: slow down, dip the lights and honk to scare off the game.

question_text:
What do you have to be aware of in this situation?
Due to the constant changing of light and shadow

options.text: - I have to drive with particular care
- I may be poorly visible to other road users
- I am more easily able to judge distances

correct_answers.text: - I have to drive with particular care
- I may be poorly visible to other road users

comment: Due to the large number of trees and the constant change between light and shade, you have to drive particularly attentively, as it is much more difficult to recognise other road users.

question_text: In the dark, an oncoming vehicle fails to dip its headlights. What can you do so that you can still see to a certain extent?

options.text: Avoid looking at the headlights of the approaching vehicle and direct your gaze towards the right-hand edge of the roadway
Also switch on full beam
Lower the sun visor

correct_answers.text: Avoid looking at the headlights of the approaching vehicle and direct your gaze towards the right-hand edge of the roadway

comment: If you are dazzled by the light from an oncoming vehicle, look to the right side of the road if possible. This reduces the dazzling effect and you can still stay the lane. It's prohibited to dazzle back by switching on the high beam. Folding down the sun shade is not an appropriate action as it will impair your vision too much.

question_text: You are driving on a country road in darkness and rain and encounter oncoming vehicles with dipped headlights. What must you remember?

options.text: You can be dazzled by reflections on the wet road
Your wet windscreen can result in your being dazzled
You can avoid possible dazzle by switching on full beam

correct_answers.text: You can be dazzled by reflections on the wet road
Your wet windscreen can result in your being dazzled

comment: You must not turn on the high beam in this situation, as this can strongly dazzle oncoming traffic. Especially on wet roads, the reflection of the light is greatly increased. Further interferences include drops of water and streaks on the windscreen, which scatter the light and cloud the view.

question_text: What risks could arise if you drive with your main beam lights on?

options.text: Oncoming road users will be dazzled
Wild animals on the road will be dazzled and will remain stationary in the light beam
Stationary vehicles on my side of the road will not be detected until it is too late

correct_answers.text: Oncoming road users will be dazzled
Wild animals on the road will be dazzled and will remain stationary in the light beam

comment: With high beam on, you can dazzle drivers in front of you and oncoming traffic, which may result in recognizing pedestrians and cyclists not at all or way too late. Game that is crossing the road can also be dazzled, which may lead to the animals remaining in the cone of light. With high beam you can recognize vehicles that broke down better.

question_text:
Driving at night-time on a rural road, you see persons on your side of the road. What do you do if you are dazzled by an oncoming vehicle?
I reduce my speed and

options.text: - look towards the right-hand side of the road
- stop if necessary
- turn on my main beam lights

correct_answers.text: - look towards the right-hand side of the road

comment: If you detect people on the side of the road at night as a car driver, you should slow down. Regular eye-contact with the roadside is ideal to avoid an accident. If you are also blinded, you can move to the right and stop.

question_text: You are driving on an avenue, with a narrow carriageway. What must you be aware of?

options.text: I may only drive at a speed that allows me to stop within half of my range of vision
Conflicts can arise with the oncoming traffic
I have to anticipate unevenness at the edge of the carriageway caused by tree roots

correct_answers.text: I may only drive at a speed that allows me to stop within half of my range of vision
Conflicts can arise with the oncoming traffic
I have to anticipate unevenness at the edge of the carriageway caused by tree roots

comment: On narrow avenues you are only allowed to drive at a speed that allows you to stop within half the visibility if oncoming traffic approaches. There may be conflicts with oncoming traffic. You may have to slow down, brake and drive to the right or reverse until the road gets wider to allow oncoming traffic drive past you. The roadside of avenues can be particularly uneven because tree roots lift the pavement.

question_text:
What increases the risk of an accident?
Driving

options.text: - with the sun low in the sky out front
- with a misted up windscreen
- with iced over side windows

correct_answers.text: - with the sun low in the sky out front

comment:
The risk of accidents is significantly increased if your windscreen and side windows are steamed up or iced over, as you can only see the traffic to a limited extent. Clear all windows before you set off.
You could also be dazzled if you drive towards the low sun. This could make you notice other road users later and increase the risk of an accident. Be extra focussed, wear sunglasses or roll down your sun visor.
